text:
cheng: Heads up — we've started seeing a spike in dropped pod connections in us-central GPU pool around 14:00 UTC. Jobs that stream model tokens hit intermittent EOFs.

marta: saw the same. model inference pods restart with 502/connection reset. any network alerts?

cheng: net-metrics shows east-west packet loss between gpufarm-uc1-az2 and az4, plus a surge of ephemeral sockets on the NAT host. suspect NAT table overcommit.

jake: @oncall can you grab conntrack counts on the node where pods fail? quick command: `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` or `cat /proc/net/nf_conntrack | wc -l`

oncall: on it. pulling counts from gpu-node-47 now.

oncall: `cat /proc/net/nf_conntrack` length = 65536 entries (conntrack_max=65536) — table at 100%

marta: that explains the resets. pods try to open many outbound connections for model prefetch and GRPC streams, everything gets SNATed through node.

cheng: digging into kube-proxy and iptables rules — saw lots of TIME_WAIT sockets and repeated short-lived connections from the batch-prefetch service.

jake: can we confirm RDMA is in play? some of the GPU pods use gDRCopy and fallback to TCP when RDMA neg fails, which would spike ephemeral ports.

cheng: RDMA sessions look stable per rdma-tool, but the fallback-to-tcp logs show bursts during model rollout: `grpc: fallback to tcp` for many clients. That coincides with a rollout around 13:58 UTC.

marta: mitigation idea: increase conntrack_max on the NAT hosts, and implement a short-lived conntrack garbage collection (reduce TIME_WAIT + more aggressive nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established) while we throttle clients.

jake: agree. also add prefix caching on the prefetch service to reduce client fanout. immediate stopgap: add conntrack sysctl bump and restart kube-proxy? risky though.

oncall: implemented sysctl change on two NAT bastions: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` — counts back to ~120k free. watching.

sre-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0347 — us-central ephemeral-socket exhaustion affecting gpu-prefetch. Pager suppressed because mitigation applied.

marta: after bump, pod restarts dropped to near-zero and GRPC errors reduced. throughput slightly lower for a few minutes as clients ramped down.

cheng: plan for a proper fix: 1) move prefetch service to use long-lived multiplexed connections (grpc keepalive + pooling), 2) enable host-level ephemeral port reuse (tcp_tw_reuse) where safe, 3) migrate some SNAT to per-pod SNAT via egress IPs to spread state, 4) add alerting when conntrack usage > 70%.

jake: can we also gate rollouts by preflight load-testing? this rollout caused traffic pattern change and pushed the table over.

marta: yes — add a Canary load-profile for model prefetch. I'll open a PR for runtime client pooling and a config change for rollout gating.

cheng: leaving this thread open for follow-ups. if anyone sees residual packet loss, ping here and I'll coordinate a sweep. :mag_right:
